summary.headline: Amagi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 27% to INR476 crores (33% ex-base), Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to INR89 crores at an 18.7% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a record revenue quarter for Amagi, with revenue of INR476 crores up 27% reported and 33% excluding a one-time rev-rec base effect of about 614 bps. Adjusted EBITDA reached INR89 crores (18.7% margin) and PAT was INR75 crores (14.9% margin). Management said margin was inflated by more than 200 bps from FX, delayed hiring and reserve releases, and guided underlying full-year margin to around 16.5%. First-half adjusted operating cash flow conversion was about 67% of Adjusted EBITDA, with INR1,774 crores of cash and no debt. Four new AI products were launched in the quarter, but management said they are not yet visible in revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +27% YoY reported; +33% ex-base; +15% reported and +21% ex-base in constant currency
vs outflow of INR98 crores a year ago

financial_highlights.value: about 151% of Adjusted EBITDA; H1 about 67%

segments.name: Cloud Modernization
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue; grew 9% reported and about 36% ex-base, with all of the base effect in this segment. Growth driven by broadcasters moving from on-prem to cloud.

segments.name: Streaming Unification
segments.commentary: About 55% of revenue; grew 35%, mostly from volume (more channels and deliveries).

segments.name: Monetization & Marketplace
segments.commentary: About 25% of revenue; grew 28%, with monetized ad impressions up 65% YoY to 16 billion.

guidance_outlook: Underlying Adjusted EBITDA margin about 16.5% for the full year after timing benefits; management expects margin to stay close to that range as operating leverage is partly reinvested in people, product and AI.
Q3 expected to be another strong quarter with elevated margins, supported by the US advertising peak and midterm elections plus recurring cloud savings.
Gross margin expected to stay in a stable 67-69% range; cloud FinOps savings were about $228,000 monthly run-rate this quarter.
Management cited a 47% incremental EBITDA flow-through as the figure to model, not 40%; a 10% USD move shifts EBITDA margin by about 1.5 pts.
R&D guided at about 20% of revenue as a steady-state number; no costs are capitalised.
No proactive quarterly guidance given beyond the margin and Q3 commentary; base case 20%-plus constant-currency growth unchanged.
Cash conversion aspiration of 50-60% for the year; H1 conversion of 67% is treated as steady state.
capex_capacity: Capex was only INR9 crores in H1, and management describes the business as capital-light.

Four new AI products launched this quarter (Amagi STUDIO, FANPULSE, Integrated Localization and Agentic NOC on Amagi Intella); NEWSPULSE is furthest along, having cleared beta, launch, paying and scaling gates.
Management said scaling new products through the paying and scaling stages will take more than one quarter.
Channel deliveries reached about 10,800, up 29% YoY; distributors 477, up 24%; content processed crossed 1 million hours, up 43%.
Corporate development is screening M&A in video supply chain, video distribution and live sports production; no binding commitment yet.
demand_pricing: Customers added: 22 in H1, about 503 total; NRR on a trailing 12-month basis about 125%, consistently above 120%.
Customers above $1 million rose to 15 from 11 a year ago; top-10 concentration about 41% of Q2 revenue, in a 39-41% band.
AI product pricing is early: moving toward fixed minimum guarantee plus consumption-based variability; currently output-based, with outcome-based pricing as a longer-term goal.
CPMs described as stabilised in the short term after compression from supply growth; management expects healthy mid-to-long-term CPMs.
Management said the cost-side and revenue-side AI products are now in the marketplace, but no AI-driven revenue has yet shown up in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term growth outlook, and does AI give more comfort on 20%-plus constant-currency growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI upside is not yet quantifiable and the base case of continuing current growth is unchanged; upside will be framed in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a headwind or tailwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called AI clearly not a headwind and potentially a large tailwind; gross margin has improved sequentially for two quarters and no top-of-funnel downsell has been seen from AI deflation.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the 40%+ flow-through, and will margins be capped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 47% flow-through is a reasonable planning figure, largely structural and not driven by currency; no artificial cuts to product and engineering costs, with reinvestment in AI expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the M&A pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are in video supply chain, distribution and live sports production; several in exploratory to preliminary diligence, nothing material this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state R&D as a share of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20% of revenue as the base case, with leverage from the platform approach; all R&D is expensed.

qa_highlights.question: What would accelerate growth beyond 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is constrained by conviction rather than financial targets; management will raise higher investment if there is high conviction, and is seeding new products for future growth.

risks_watch: Quality of margin: management said Q2 margin was inflated by more than 200 bps from FX, delayed hiring and reserve releases, so underlying margin is about 16.5%.
Cash conversion is lumpy: Q2 was about 151% but H1 is 67%, and Q1 is seasonally weakest.
Revenue base effect: the 614 bps rev-rec benefit in last year's Q2 will not repeat, so reported growth will be lower than ex-base growth in H1.
Execution on AI product scaling: four products are still at beta or launch and their revenue contribution is not yet visible.
Leadership transition and hiring: senior GTM and AI-talent hires, plus proposed board additions (Dr. Bhaskar Ghosh and co-founder Srividhya Srinivasan) subject to shareholder approval.
CPM and seasonality risk to gross margin in the US Q3 advertising peak.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter and AI, describing it as a record quarter with tailwinds. Management was more cautious on forward numbers, repeatedly saying AI revenue upside is too early to quantify and that they are "not running victory laps". Where questioned on investment and growth beyond 20%, answers were hedged and deferred to future quarters.
key_quotes: Revenue was a record INR476 crores, up 27% year-on-year. And if you exclude the one-time item in the base that we had, it's 33%.
Excluding these timing benefits, our underlying margin was closer to 16.5%. For the full year, we expect margin to stay close to that range.
Moving new products through the scaling phase will take more than one quarter, so it's going to take some time, and it won't be a quarter-on-quarter progression that you see.
I think 20% would be a reasonable steady-state number.

growth.why: Management reiterated a 20%+ constant-currency base-case growth aspiration with no quarterly revenue guidance; growth is backed by volume gains (channels +29%, NRR ~125%) and new AI products not yet visible in revenue, with no specific capacity additions disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Underlying FY27 Adjusted EBITDA margin guided to about 16.5% versus Q2's 18.7% reported, which was inflated by more than 200 bps from FX, delayed hiring and reserve releases; H1 margin is 15.3%, and Q3 is expected to be strong but reinvestment in people, product and AI caps expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management describes the business as capital-light with H1 capex of only INR9 crores, and no new physical capacity was discussed; growth is driven by channel deliveries (about 10,800, up 29%) on existing infrastructure.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume is compounding: channel deliveries up 29% to about 10,800, distributors up 24% to 477, content processed up 43% past 1 million hours, monetized ad impressions up 65% to 16 billion, and NRR about 125%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was INR9 crores in H1 against INR1,774 crores of cash with no debt, and utilisation was not disclosed as a constraint, so no capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no proactive quarterly guidance and held the 20%-plus constant-currency base case unchanged, while calling the Q2 margin flattered by one-offs and guiding full-year underlying margin to about 16.5%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 margin of 18.7% included more than 200 bps of FX, hiring-delay and reserve-release benefits that will not repeat, and reported growth will fall as the 614 bps base effect rolls off; a 10% USD move shifts margin by about 1.5 pts.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four AI products (Amagi STUDIO, FANPULSE, Integrated Localization, Agentic NOC on Intella) launched this quarter, with NEWSPULSE furthest along; management said scaling through paying and scaling stages takes more than one quarter, and revenue impact is not yet visible.

rows.label: AI product monetisation ramp
rows.why: Pricing is moving to fixed minimum guarantee plus consumption, but management says no AI-driven revenue has shown up yet and quantification is too early, so upside is unproven.

rows.label: Cloud FinOps savings
rows.why: Cloud FinOps savings reached about $228,000 monthly run-rate this quarter, supporting gross margin in the stable 67-69% range and the Q3 margin strength.

rows.label: M&A in video supply chain and live sports
rows.why: Several targets are in exploratory to preliminary diligence with no binding commitment and nothing material this quarter, so any deal is conditional.
